problem: Object-goal navigation only brings a robot within 1-2 m of the target, which is not a manipulation-ready base pose. Prior last-mile methods need manual pose annotation or task-specific training, and zero-shot MLLM pipelines (e.g. MoTo) use only object-level cues, which cannot satisfy fine-grained spatial constraints.
motivation: Mobile manipulation needs the base to end in a pose that is reachable, collision-free and suited to the manipulation. Open-vocabulary tasks with spatial relations such as 'in front of the monitor' need task-aware spatial reasoning rather than object localization. MLLMs are strong visual-spatial reasoners, but they are weak at inferring metric geometry from a 2D image alone.
key_idea: Decompose zero-shot last-mile navigation into view selection, task-conditioned affordance grounding and geometry-aware base-pose reasoning, all done by one shared MLLM, with the grounded affordance lifted to 3D and given to the MLLM as explicit geometry.
insight: Explicit geometry matters: removing base-pose reasoning (the MLLM grounds a floor point directly from 2D) substantially hurts Pick and Overall SR. Computing heading geometrically instead of asking the MLLM raises Overall SR from 17.08 to 25.42. Splitting view selection and grounding into separate calls beats merging them (Gemini Overall SR drops 4.17 points when merged). Base-pose reasoning is the stage that benefits most from a thinking model (Qwen3-VL-8B Overall SR 9.58 to 20.83), and a 4B robotics-tuned MLLM (RoboBrain-2.5-4B) beats much larger general MLLMs.
method: View selection: keeps a buffer of the last K=5 observations and robot states from the end of object navigation. The MLLM picks one reference view using two criteria: the target is clearly visible, and a feasible approach path exists.

Task-conditioned affordance grounding: given the selected view and the instruction, the MLLM outputs a normalized 2D affordance point (u,v). For pick, this is a graspable point on the object. For place, it is a safe, stable, interior placement point on the receptacle. Qwen3-VL and RoboBrain use their native 0-1000 coordinate format.

3D lifting and visual prompting: the point is lifted with the aligned depth map and camera parameters into the robot-centric frame of the selected pose, giving p_a. It is also marked on the image as a red dot.

Geometry-aware base-pose reasoning: the MLLM receives the marked image, p_a, robot configuration and task, and predicts the base position (x,y). It aims for 70-80% of max arm reach and avoids collisions. It also outputs arm reach and lift for a simple placement policy.
Geometric heading: theta is computed by turning the robot toward the lifted affordance point rather than predicted by the MLLM.

Execution: the local pose is transformed to the global frame and passed to a low-level navigation policy (HomeRobot default in sim, Nav2 on the real robot). The real robot adds an affordance refinement step using the wrist camera.

setting.backbone: Gemini-3-Flash-Preview (frozen, main); also GPT-4.1/5.2/5.4, Qwen3-VL, Qwen3.5/3.6, InternVL3.5, RoboBrain-2.0-7B/2.5-4B (frozen)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D, proprioception, odometry, obstacle map
setting.action_space: base pose (x,y,theta) target passed to a low-level navigation policy; arm extension and lift height predicted by the MLLM
setting.privileged: none stated beyond the assumed pre-built scene map and an object-navigation policy that reaches the target vicinity

numbers.extra: default HomeRobot navigation and grasping policies; MLLM-predicted arm settings for placement

numbers_note: Benchmark is HomeRobot OVMM; mapped to canonical name HomeRobot-OVMM. The framework-ablation figure (w/o last-mile navigation below 5% Overall SR) is only in a figure and text. Real-world result: 7/10, 6/10, 4/10, 4/10 on four tasks, 52.5% total.
results: On the OVMM validation set, UniLM-Nav with Gemini-3-Flash-Preview reaches 23.77% Overall SR, beating the previous SOTA MoTo (20.64%), the training-based MoManipVLA (15.80%) and UniTeam (17.96%). The 4B RoboBrain-2.5 variant gets 19.19%. In real-world tests on a Unitree B2+Z1, it succeeds on 52.5% of trials, weaker on fine spatial-relation tasks.
limitations: Assumes object navigation already brings the target into recent observations. Navigation errors are 61.0% of failures, and last-mile errors 20.9%.
Failures come from view selection, affordance grounding (points near edges) and base-pose reasoning; MLLM spatial reasoning is the bottleneck for fine-grained spatial instructions in the real world.
Evaluated only on OVMM, with ablations on a 20% subset, and real-world tests are small (10 trials per task).
